html:
In 2017 scientists announced that human fossils from Jebel Irhoud, a cave site in western Morocco, were about 300,000 years old. That made them the oldest known remains of Homo sapiens.

The first bones were found there by miners in 1961. New digs led by Jean-Jacques Hublin found skulls, jaws and stone tools, and dated them by the burnt flints. The faces looked much like ours, while the braincases were longer and lower.

Until then the oldest fossils of our species came from Ethiopia and were about 100,000 years younger. The find suggested that modern humans evolved across the whole of Africa, not in one corner of it. See also human evolution and Morocco.
